name: TWELVE MKII
notes: USB-MIDI class compliant: the controls appear as a generic MIDI device, no driver needed. Rane publishes no public CC/note table, so these tests learn each control's message live and record it in the results; that record becomes the reference map for this database. No USB audio: DVS signal leaves via the RCA outputs.

drivers.name: TWELVE MKII Firmware Updater (firmware 00.53, Windows v1.0.2)

serviceManual.notes: No public service manual. Rane/inMusic supply service documentation only to authorized Rane service centers.

setup: Connect USB-B directly to the computer (or a powered hub / Rane mixer hub) and mains power.
Close Serato/VirtualDJ so MIDItest can see the raw MIDI.
Put a record on the slipmat. Select Deck 1 so the MIDI channel stays the same during the tests.
failureModes: Pitch fader off-centre or not reaching full range (recalibrate: hold 8%+16% at power-on)
Platter reversing or changing speed on fast pull-back + Start/Stop (old motor firmware)

tests.name: MIDI port appears
steps: Press Enable MIDI, open this device and confirm the Device MIDI in list shows a TWELVE MKII port.
Write the exact port name into the notes field.

tests.name: Any MIDI arrives
steps: Press any button or touch the platter. Five or more messages = pass.

tests.name: Platter motion both directions
steps: Motor OFF. Turn the platter slowly forwards one full turn, then backwards one full turn.
Both directions must be detected. Look for gaps or bursts in the message rate.

tests.name: Fast scratch / data continuity
steps: Motor ON at 33. Scratch back and forth quickly for about 10 seconds.
Watch for dropouts. The message count must keep climbing with no stalls.

tests.name: Motor, speed and torque
steps: Press Start/Stop. The platter should reach 33⅓ smoothly. Check speed with a strobe or a phone strobe app.
Switch to 45 and check again. Pitch at 0% must match the strobe.
Toggle torque Hi/Lo: the drag under your hand should change clearly.
Motor Off switch: the platter should wind down. Fast pull-back + Start/Stop: the platter must not reverse or jump speed.

tests.name: Pitch fader full travel
steps: Move the pitch fader slowly from one end to the other, then back.
It must reach both extremes with no jumps. If it uses 14-bit pitch-bend, the range check scales automatically.

tests.name: Pitch range buttons 8/16/50%
steps: Press 8%, 16% and 50% in turn. Each must send a message and change the OLED range.

tests.name: Pitch centre / calibration
steps: Put the fader in the centre detent. The OLED should show 0.0%.
If it doesn't: power on holding 8% + 16% (Test Mode), move full left, full right, centre, press 8% + 50%, power-cycle.

tests.name: Start/Stop and deck buttons
steps: Press and release Start/Stop (motor may start: that's fine), then each Deck Select button.
Each must send press AND release.

tests.name: Touch strip – search & 8 cue zones
steps: Slide a finger along the whole strip slowly, end to end, then tap each of the 8 cue zones.
Values should cover the full length. Note any dead spots in the notes field.

tests.name: Browse encoder + push
steps: Turn the browse encoder 5+ clicks each way. Push it and press Back / Instant Doubles.

tests.name: Every remaining button
steps: Press each remaining button on the deck once (Back, Instant Doubles, shift-type buttons, strip mode, etc.).
Adjust the count in your notes if your unit has more or fewer.

tests.name: LED feedback (echo learned buttons)
steps: Select the Device MIDI out.
Press Send: MIDItest sends the button messages back at full value. Note which LEDs light. Some feedback is SysEx/host-only, so 'no response' is a finding, not a fail.

tests.name: OLED display
steps: Check the OLED for dead pixels or lines and that it shows pitch range and deck.
Optional: load Serato and confirm BPM appears (firmware 00.53+ for VirtualDJ).

tests.name: RCA output / DVS signal
steps: Connect the RCA outputs to a mixer or interface. Play the control signal or record.
Check both channels for hum, crackle or one-sided output.
